command: claude CLI 2.1.285 print mode (claude -p --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --no-session-persistence --system-prompt <porting system prompt>, prompt file on stdin, run from an empty directory)
notes:
Defects / behaviours of the original kept:
- EVALUATE WS-MODE has no WHEN OTHER. An unknown or blank mode starts nothing but still sends
  'STARTS ISSUED'. Fix: add WHEN OTHER with a SEND TEXT such as 'INVALID MODE'.
- RECEIVE has no RESP/NOHANDLE/HANDLE CONDITION. Terminal input longer than 20 bytes (including the
  transid) raises LENGERR, which abends the task with AEIV. Fix: add RESP(WS-RESP) to the RECEIVE
  and test it.
- The STARTs have no RESP either. Any non-NORMAL condition takes the default action, an abend
  through task.abendOnCondition. CicsTask.abcodeFor knows INVREQ and LENGERR only. If TRANSIDERR or
  TERMIDERR ever occurred it would raise IllegalArgumentException instead. I did not invent an abend
  code for those; GT02 is defined in the CSD per the navigation facts.
- Mode X: the ABEND at line 58 is ported as task.abend("GTAB"), as rule 14 requires, and the task
  ends there. The generated abendGtabL58() is kept unchanged but not called from runTask.
- WS-INLEN is set by RECEIVE but never used afterwards.

Assumptions / facts:
- START FROM data is passed as the field's bytes in EBCDIC (IBM037), the region's code page.
  CicsTask documents this for TS items; for START it is my assumption.
- executeGtstart has no batch step to port (a CICS-only program, no COMMAREA per the interface
  facts), so it only logs.
- No fact was contradicted by the source. The field-testing-open sections (calls, cics_tasks,
  navigation) match lines 34-58.
- The "commarea_length" values in the calls facts are the START FROM LENGTHs, not a COMMAREA.
